open.item: The Company signed a sub-lease agreement with Alborz Developers Limited to set up the first Time Out Market in Delhi and announced it as an immersive food and cultural destination.
Having amended its object clause, the Company intends to expand beyond digital media into hospitality and food services, cultural and experiential ventures and real estate activities.
Management commits that media-tech will remain the Company's focal area as part of its long-term strategy despite diversification into new segments.

open.horizon: Time Out India live; Delhi market lease signed
open.item: The Company entered the hospitality segment through an exclusive franchise agreement with Time Out Group, UK, launching Time Out India as a digital city guide and signing a lease for the first Time Out India Market in Delhi.

Management states that the Quintype India and Quintype Technologies Inc. (ListenFirst) subsidiaries, which contributed significantly to the Company's top and bottom lines in FY26, are anticipated to continue doing so in future.

The Company amended its Memorandum of Association object clause, approved by the Registrar of Companies on October 3, 2025, to enable operations in hospitality and food services, cultural and experiential ventures, and real estate activities.

risks.note: The only BRSR material issue the Company classifies as a Risk with negative financial implications. As a digital platform, a breach can compromise customer information and the Company's content; mitigation is a strict IT policy adhered to at all times plus a dedicated IT team constantly monitoring security processes.

Listed first under Threats in the MD&A Opportunities and Threats section - media companies are witnessing revenue drops (the disclosure is truncated in the routed text), and the Company competes in ad-supported niches where competition is explicitly acknowledged.
risks.risk: Thinning margins across the media industry

risks.note: Exports contributed 78.86% of the entity's total turnover per BRSR Section A, so the bulk of income depends on overseas clients and geographies (principally the US media-tech business), exposing the Company to foreign-currency and offshore-demand shifts.

BRSR discloses that 90% of turnover comes from a single main activity - other information and communication service activities, specifically operation of websites acting as internet portals with periodically updated content - leaving little revenue diversification within the listed entity.

The business is people-led (content, editorial and engineering). Permanent-employee turnover was 21.79% in FY 2025-2026, an improvement on 55.72% in FY 2024-2025 and 42.96% in FY 2023-2024, but historically elevated attrition remains a structural exposure.

BRSR states that as a digital company the core asset is the hardware and infrastructure that powers The Quint, and the Company heavily depends on energy to maintain operations; it is framed as an opportunity to be addressed through energy-efficient equipment, but the underlying dependence is structural.

The MD&A notes monetization is shifting from linear TV to digital, that legacy players are restructuring portfolios and spinning off digital-first entities, and that over 50 players are consolidating around high-value original content - management explicitly recognises disruption as a fundamental architecture of the M&E sector requiring agility and continuous reinvention.
risks.risk: Structural disruption of the media and entertainment business model

risks.note: The Company amended its object clause to enter hospitality and food services, cultural and experiential ventures and real estate, and signed a sub-lease for the first Time Out Market in Delhi - businesses materially different in operating model from its asset-light digital media and media-tech base.
